acceptance_condition: A compact answer (<=6 claims) defining argumentation framework, attack, admissibility, and the grounded/preferred/stable extensions with their existence/uniqueness guarantees, plus an explicit note on what the framework cannot represent; each claim with an explicit `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker.
rationale: Dung provides the formal semantics for when a synthesized conclusion is justified under conflict — the 'synthesis competence' node of the D3 causal model. The wave-1 combined Dung+Shapiro investigation likely failed because two papers in one packet produced an oversized output; this single-paper split halves the scope.
text: From Dung 1995 (papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt) only: extract the formal machinery relevant to adjudicating conflicting agent answers — argumentation frameworks, attack relations, conflict-free/admissible sets, and the grounded/preferred/stable extensions with what each guarantees about justified conclusions — and state explicitly what the framework does NOT model (evidential weight, truth, probabilistic confidence). Keep the answer compact: at most 6 claims, each with a `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker.
